summary: geant4_benchmarks.py applied its heavy-particle references (Bethe mean rate, RPP eq. 34.5; Landau-Vavilov Delta_p and xi, eq. 34.12) to electrons and positrons in stopping-power, thin-layer-mpv, thin-layer-width and the reference command; they now refuse e- and e+.

observables: reference_value and verdict of stopping-power, thin-layer-mpv and thin-layer-width benchmarks for e- and e+
the numbers of the reference command for e- and e+
impact.bias: Bethe with W_max = T gave 1.4865 MeV cm2/g at gamma 3.3 for both e- and e+ in silicon, where RPP prints 1.50 (e-) and 1.46 (e+, gamma 3.7); the mean loss of a 100 MeV electron in 0.3 mm of silicon includes about 0.32 MeV of bremsstrahlung against a 0.130 MeV reference, so a correct Geant4 run failed the reference benchmark
impact.trigger: a stopping-power, thin-layer-mpv or thin-layer-width benchmark, or the reference command, with particle e- or e+

applies_to.match_basis: a Geant4 study record (check_geant4_study.py) embeds the benchmark results of geant4_benchmarks.py in extension.study.benchmarks; a record that lists one of these benchmarks was evaluated by the affected code

outputs.how_to_recognize: geant4_benchmarks.py run or reference output (JSON) for particle e- or e+ (the run's benchmarks[*].scope.particle, the reference command's inputs.particle)

remedy: electron and positron energy-loss studies need a reference stated for e+- (collision stopping power, RPP eqs. 34.23-34.24, plus bremsstrahlung, or a published measurement through published-data); rerunning with this version refuses them (exit 2)
